mainTopic: How to read a dying man's instructions and a field set aside for a widow's support, then the start of a new chapter: a husband may add to the כתובה, and the extra counts as the כתובה itself.
overview: The amud opens with a short case. A father said to give his daughter 400 זוז worth of wine, the wine went up in value, and רב יוסף rules that the extra goes to the יתומים. Next comes a story about רבי יוחנן's relatives, whose father's wife spent too much on her support. רבי יוחנן advised setting aside a field for her, but ריש לקיש ruled that this only added to her support, and רבי יוחנן said he could not overrule an equal. רבי אבהו then explains that it depends on the wording: "לִמְזוֹנוֹת" adds to her support, while "בִּמְזוֹנוֹת" caps it. After the הדרן closing פרק נערה, a new משנה teaches that a husband may add any amount to the basic כתובה. The משנה also records disputes about collecting the extra after אירוסין and about lowering the basic amount. The גמרא explains why the משנה had to say adding is allowed. It then learns from the word 'add' that the extra counts as the כתובה itself, which matters in six practical cases.

steps.title: Wine set aside for the daughter goes up in value
steps.stepSummary: A father said to give his daughter 400 זוזים from his wine. The wine rose in value, and רב יוסף rules that the extra value goes to the יתומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Give four hundred זוז from the wine to my daughter." The wine went up in value. רב יוסף said: the gain goes to the orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case about a father's instruction to give his daughter 400 זוזים' worth of wine, and רב יוסף rules on who keeps the extra when the wine's price goes up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father set a money amount (400 זוזים), not an amount of wine. So the daughter gets exactly 400 זוזים' worth. Whatever is left after the price rise stays with the heirs, the יתומים.

keyTerms.meaning: זוז coins, a unit of money
Wine
Became more expensive, went up in value
The gain, the profit
The orphans, meaning the heirs

phrases.english: "Four hundred zuz from the wine, to my daughter."
The wine went up in value.
Rav Yosef said:
The gain goes to the orphans.
phrases.notes: "The orphans" here are the sons who inherit the father's estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי מִן חַמְרָא לִבְרַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a series of cases from before this section about how to read a father's instructions to his heirs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the instruction is 400 זוזים' worth of wine and the wine goes up in value, the daughter gets only 400 זוזים' worth, and the extra goes to the יתומים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן advises setting aside land for a wasteful wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's relatives complain that their father's wife spends too much on her support. רבי יוחנן advises that their father set aside a field for her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן's relatives had a wife of their father who was wasting money on her support. They came to רבי יוחנן. He told them: Go tell your father to set aside land for her support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. Relatives of רבי יוחנן ask him how to deal with their father's wife, who spends too much on her מזונות (support).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's plan is that a specific field would be marked for her support. The idea is that her support would come from that field, which would protect the rest of the estate. The next steps test whether this plan really works.

keyTerms.meaning: His relatives
The father's wife
Wastes, causes a loss
Food and support
He should set aside, designate
Land, a field

phrases.english: The relatives of Rabbi Yochanan
had a wife of their father
who was wasting money on her support.
They came before Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to them:
Go and tell your father
that he should set aside land for her support.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה לְהוּ אִיתַּת אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about a man who sets aside land for his wife's מזונות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן advises that the father set aside a field for his wife's support, in order to protect the rest of the estate.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the land only adds to her support
steps.stepSummary: After the father dies, the relatives ask ריש לקיש. He rules that setting aside the field gives her even more support, not less.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before ריש לקיש. He said to them: All the more so, he has increased her support.
steps.whatsHappening: The relatives bring the case to ריש לקיש. He gives the opposite result from what רבי יוחנן's plan was meant to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ריש לקיש's view, setting aside a field does not replace her regular support. It is an extra source added on top. So the heirs must still support her in full, and the field becomes a backup.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
All the more so
He increased, added more

phrases.english: They came before Reish Lakish,
He said to them:
All the more so, he has increased her support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that goes against the intended result of רבי יוחנן's advice in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting aside land for the wife's support adds to her support. It does not limit it.

steps.title: The relatives object: רבי יוחנן did not say that
steps.stepSummary: The relatives push back against ריש לקיש by pointing out that רבי יוחנן did not rule this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But רבי יוחנן did not say so!
steps.whatsHappening: The relatives challenge ריש לקיש by pointing to רבי יוחנן's advice, which was meant to protect the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their challenge rests on authority, not on a new argument. They expected the field to limit her support, because that was why רבי יוחנן suggested it.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, but surely (opens a challenge)
Did not say so

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר הָכִי!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan did not say so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that the field adds to her support
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן advised setting aside the field in order to limit her spending, so ריש לקיש's ruling seems to go against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש insists they must support her
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש stands by his ruling and warns the relatives that he will push them hard if they do not obey.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Go give her. And if not, I will take רבי יוחנן out of your ears.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש does not back down. He orders them to give her full support and warns them strongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue against רבי יוחנן's view. He simply rules firmly as a judge. His sharp expression shows how sure he is of his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Go give her
And if not
I will take out, remove
Your ears

phrases.english: He said to them: Go and give her.
And if not,
I will take Rabbi Yochanan out of your ears.
phrases.notes: A sharp saying. He means he will deal with them so harshly that they will forget רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 4 by insisting on the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש keeps his ruling. The heirs must give her full support.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: an equal disagrees with me
steps.stepSummary: The relatives go back to רבי יוחנן. He says he cannot override ריש לקיש, because ריש לקיש is his equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבי יוחנן. He said to them: What can I do? For one equal to me disagrees with me.
steps.whatsHappening: The relatives complain to רבי יוחנן. He tells them he cannot overturn the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן admits that ריש לקיש is a scholar of his own level. When an equal disagrees with him, he will not cancel the other's ruling. That leaves ריש לקיש's ruling in place for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do?
One who is equal to me, my match
Disagrees with me

phrases.english: They came before Rabbi Yochanan,
He said to them: What can I do?
For one equal to me disagrees with me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story. רבי יוחנן declines to overturn ריש לקיש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן will not override his equal, so ריש לקיש's ruling stands in this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It leaves it looking as if רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש truly disagree. That sets up רבי אבהו's explanation in the next step.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: it depends on the exact wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports that רבי יוחנן explained it to him personally. Saying "לִמְזוֹנוֹת" (for support) adds to her support. Saying "בִּמְזוֹנוֹת" (as support) fixes her support at that field alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It was explained to me by רבי יוחנן himself. If he said "for support," he increased her support. If he said "as support," he fixed her support.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו reports רבי יוחנן's own explanation. It shows that the outcome depends on the exact words the husband used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לִמְזוֹנוֹת" means the field is an extra source added on top of her regular support, as ריש לקיש ruled. "בִּמְזוֹנוֹת" means the field is her support, and she gets nothing beyond it. That is the result רבי יוחנן's advice was aiming for. So the two rulings fit two different wordings.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me
For support (an added source)
As support (the full amount)
He fixed, set a limit

steps.whatToRemember: "לִמְזוֹנוֹת" (for support) means the land is an extra source, and she still gets full support. "בִּמְזוֹנוֹת" (as support) means the land is all she gets. One letter changes the whole ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. "לִמְזוֹנוֹת" sounds like it should limit her, but it is the one that increases her support. "בִּמְזוֹנוֹת" is the one that caps it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that the exact words used when setting up support decide whether the heirs owe more than the field.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: To me personally it was explained by Rabbi Yochanan.
If he said "for support,"
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband who set aside the field for his wife.

phrases.english: he has increased her support.
If he said "as support,"
he has fixed her support.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the apparent disagreement between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש in steps 2 to 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Saying "לִמְזוֹנוֹת" adds the field on top of her support. Saying "בִּמְזוֹנוֹת" makes the field her only support.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of נערה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line marks the end of the fourth chapter of כתובות, פרק נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter נערה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the chapter of נערה with the traditional farewell line. Nothing new is being argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a closing formula that expresses our wish to come back and learn this chapter again. Here it closes the chapter, whose last cases dealt with a father's instructions to his heirs and a widow's support from the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the line said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter just finished, taken from its first word

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter Na'arah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose last story was concluded in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Chapter נערה is complete, and a new chapter begins.

steps.title: The husband may add to the כתובה, and when the extra amount is collected
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a husband may add any amount to the basic כתובה. The תנא קמא says she collects the full amount whether the marriage ends at אירוסין or נישואין. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says that from אירוסין she collects only the basic amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the rule is that a בתולה collects 200 and an אלמנה collects 100, if the husband wants to add, even 10,000, he may. If she is widowed or divorced, whether from אירוסין or from נישואין, she collects everything. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: from נישואין she collects everything, but from אירוסין a בתולה collects 200 and an אלמנה 100, because he only wrote the extra in order to marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה teaching that the basic כתובה is only a minimum, so the husband may add to it. The משנה then records a disagreement about when the extra amount is actually collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that adding is allowed. The argument is about a marriage that ends after אירוסין but before נישואין. The תנא קמא says the extra is owed anyway. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the extra was a gift meant for a completed marriage, so if they never got to נישואין she gets only the basic amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hundred זוז, the basic כתובה of a בתולה
One hundred זוז, the basic כתובה of an אלמנה
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage before she enters his home
Full marriage, the second stage
On condition of bringing her into the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not say the basic 200 or 100 is lost after אירוסין. He only says the EXTRA amount is not collected.

phrases.english: Although they said
a virgin collects two hundred
and a widow one maneh
if he wishes to add
even a hundred maneh, he may add
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 זוז, so a hundred מנה comes to ten thousand.

phrases.english: If she was widowed or divorced

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין
phrases.english: whether from betrothal or from marriage
she collects everything
phrases.notes: Everything means the basic amount plus the extra he added.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says
from marriage, she collects everything

phrases.aramaic: מִן הָאֵירוּסִין — בְּתוּלָה גּוֹבָה מָאתַיִם וְאַלְמָנָה מָנֶה
phrases.english: from betrothal, a virgin collects two hundred and a widow one maneh
for he only wrote it for her
on condition of marrying her

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתוּלָה גּוֹבָה מָאתַיִם וְאַלְמָנָה מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband may add any amount to the basic כתובה. According to the תנא קמא the full amount is collected even from אירוסין. According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, from אירוסין only the basic amount is collected.

steps.title: Can the wife give up part of her basic כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the wife may write a receipt for money she never received, so in effect she lowers her basic כתובה. רבי מאיר says that anyone who lowers the כתובה below the minimum turns the marriage into בעילת זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if he wishes, he writes a בתולה a document for 200, and she writes 'I received a מנה from you.' For an אלמנה he writes 100, and she writes 'I received fifty זוז from you.' רבי מאיר says: anyone who gives a בתולה less than 200, or an אלמנה less than 100, his relationship with her is בעילת זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on to a second dispute. The question now is whether the basic amount can be made smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats the basic כתובה as the wife's right, so she may give part of it up with a receipt for money she never got. רבי מאיר holds that the minimum may never be lowered. If it is lowered, it is as if there is no כתובה at all, so living together counts as בעילת זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A written legal document
I have received, the wording of a receipt
A silver coin, the same as a dinar
One who reduces or gives less
A forbidden relationship treated like one without proper marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute shows two views of the basic כתובה. רבי יהודה sees it as the wife's money right, which she can give up. רבי מאיר sees it as a fixed minimum that may never be lowered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says
if he wishes, he writes for a virgin
a document of two hundred
and she writes
'I received a maneh from you'
phrases.notes: She never actually got this money. The receipt is her way of giving up half.

phrases.english: and for a widow, a maneh
and she writes 'I received fifty zuz from you'
Rabbi Meir says
anyone who gives a virgin less than two hundred
or a widow less than a maneh
this is licentious relations

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם רָצָה כּוֹתֵב לִבְתוּלָה שְׁטָר שֶׁל מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 9 dealt with raising the כתובה. This step deals with lowering it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the wife may give up part of her basic כתובה through a receipt. רבי מאיר: lowering the minimum makes the relationship בעילת זנות.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that he may add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's first ruling. Of course a person may promise more money if he wants to, so why teach it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking why the משנה needed to say that a husband may add to the כתובה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may always take on extra debts with his own money, so the rule seems too obvious to need saying. The challenge is aimed at why the משנה teaches it at all, not at the rule itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
It is obvious, a challenge asking why something needed to be said

phrases.english: Gemara: Isn't it obvious?
phrases.notes: The obvious point is the משנה's first ruling, that he may add to the כתובה if he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first ruling of the משנה in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement 'אם רצה להוסיף יוסיף'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person may always choose to promise more of his own money, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought the רבנן set a fixed amount to protect the poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the רבנן set a fixed כתובה amount for everyone, so that poor people would not be embarrassed. The משנה teaches that there is no such limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the רבנן made a fixed amount so as not to embarrass someone who does not have money. So the משנה teaches us that he may add.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to teach that adding is allowed. It shows there was a reasonable mistake the משנה wanted to prevent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought there was a fixed ceiling, so that rich men could not give big כתובות and make poor men look bad. The משנה teaches that the רבנן set only a minimum, not a maximum, so adding is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, introducing a mistaken idea
A fixed, set amount or limit
To embarrass
It teaches us, introducing the correct conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: The basic כתובה amounts are a minimum, not a maximum. The גמרא shows the ruling 'he may add' was needed, because we might have thought the רבנן set a fixed amount to protect the poor from embarrassment.

phrases.english: Lest you say
the Rabbis made a fixed amount

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ
phrases.english: so as not to embarrass one who does not have
phrases.notes: He means a man who cannot afford a large כתובה.

phrases.english: it teaches us

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא, showing that the ruling prevents a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן fixed one amount for everyone so poor men would not be embarrassed.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no upper limit, so the husband may add as much as he wants.

steps.title: Reading the משנה's word 'add' closely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'if he wants to add' and points out that the משנה chose the word 'add' instead of 'write for her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he wants to add, etc.' Notice that it does not say 'if he wants to write for her.' It says 'if he wants to add.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the משנה and points out an exact word choice. This sets up the next step, where the word choice will be used as support for an אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing a separate promise would mean a new, independent debt. 'Adding' means the extra money joins the כתובה and becomes part of it. So the extra money should follow the same rules as the basic כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: to add (the extra money becomes part of the כתובה)
it does not teach / the משנה did not say
to write for her (a separate written promise)

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] 'If he wants to add, etc.'
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points back to the משנה from Step 9: he may add even a very large amount.

phrases.english: It does not say 'if he wants to write for her,'
rather, 'if he wants to add.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָצָה לִכְתּוֹב לָהּ לָא קָתָנֵי אֶלָּא רָצָה לְהוֹסִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening words of the משנה (Step 9) for a new close reading, after the קשיא and תירוץ of Steps 11–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's word 'add' shows that the extra amount is joined to the כתובה itself and is not a separate promise.

steps.title: This supports רבי ינאי: the extras count as the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The word 'add' supports רבי איבו in the name of רבי ינאי, who rules that תנאי כתובה are treated like the כתובה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports what רבי איבו said in the name of רבי ינאי. רבי איבו said in the name of רבי ינאי: The extras of the כתובה are like the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה's wording backs up a ruling of רבי ינאי. The extras a husband adds to the כתובה count as the כתובה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that the extra money is 'added' onto the כתובה. That is exactly רבי ינאי's point: the extra amount gets the same legal treatment as the basic כתובה. The משנה is the source, and רבי ינאי's rule is what it supports.

keyTerms.meaning: it supports him (a source that backs up an אמורא's view)
the extras of the כתובה (here, the extra amount the husband adds)
is treated like the כתובה itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for the whole list of practical cases that comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: Elsewhere, תנאי כתובה can mean the built-in obligations of the כתובה, like food and burial. Here the גמרא is talking about the extra money the husband adds.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַיְבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי.
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Aivu, [who] said in the name of Rabbi Yannai.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַיְבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Aivu said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
The extras of the marriage contract are like the marriage contract itself.

steps.title: Six cases where the rule makes a difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists six cases where the extra amount follows the same rules as the basic כתובה: מוכרת, מוחלת, מורדת, פוגמת, תובעת, and עוברת על דת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is for: a woman who sells her כתובה, a woman who waives it, a woman who rebels, a woman who says she was partly paid, a woman who demands payment, and a woman who breaks the rules of proper Jewish conduct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי ינאי's rule matters in real life. It lists six situations where the extra money is treated the same as the basic כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, whatever happens to the basic כתובה also happens to the extra amount. A sale or a waiver includes it. A מורדת has it reduced. A פוגמת must swear to collect it. A תובעת loses her support once she claims it. An עוברת על דת is sent away without it.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical difference that comes out of it
a wife who rebels and refuses her husband
a woman who admits she already received part of her כתובה
a woman who demands payment of her כתובה
a woman who breaks הלכה or proper Jewish conduct

steps.whatToRemember: The extra money a husband adds to the כתובה is not a side promise. It is part of the כתובה and follows all its rules: selling, waiving, losing it, and swearing for it.

phrases.english: The practical difference is:
for a woman who sells [her כתובה], and for one who waives [it];
phrases.notes: If she sells or waives her כתובה, the extra amount goes along with it automatically.

phrases.english: for a rebellious wife, and for one who admits partial payment;
phrases.notes: Money taken off a מורדת's כתובה comes off the extra too. A פוגמת must swear before collecting the rest, extra included.

phrases.english: for one who demands [payment], and for one who breaks the rules of proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical results of רבי ינאי's rule from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the extras count as the כתובה, they are included in every rule about the כתובה: sale, waiver, reduction for a מורדת, an oath for a פוגמת, loss of support for a תובעת, and loss of the כתובה for an עוברת על דת.
